sentences.text: The Applicant has filed this Application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for enlarging the Applicant on Regular Bail in connection with FIR being C.R. No. 11195007230573 of 2023 registered with Bhabhar Police Station, Banaskantha for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(3), 506(2) of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 and 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned Advocate for the Applicant and learned APP for the Respondent - State.
3.
Learned Advocate for the Applicant submitted that the Applicant has been arrested in connection with the present offence on 19.08.2023 and since then the Applicant is in custody.
The Aplicant has been falsely implicated in the present offence.
Earlier the Applicant has filed Criminal Miscellaneous Application No. 22005 of 2023 which was allowed to be withdrawn vide order dated 12.12.2023.

While allowing to withdraw the Application, liberty was granted to the Applicant to file Application Surajsinh Vajubha Rathod vs State Of Gujarat on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24819231/
1 afresh after a period of eight months if the trial did not progress satisfactorily during the said period.

sentences.text: R/CR.MA/24129/2024 ORDER
Learned Advocate for the Applicant further submitted that the case of the prosecution is absolutely concocted and the Applicant has been made a victim of a well-organized plan by the prosecution.
He further submits that the Applicant is a student aged 19 Years.

Learned Advocate for the Applicant has further submitted that the Applicant has good reputation in the society and no useful purpose would be served by keeping the applicant in jail for indefinite period.
It is further contended that the applicant is ready and willing to abide by all the conditions that may be imposed by this Court if released on bail.

4. Per contra, learned APP has opposed the present application for grant of regular bail and submitted that looking to the nature of offence, this Court may not exercise the discretion in favour of the applicant and the Application may be dismissed.
5. Heard learned Advocates for the parties and perused the record.

The Applicant had earlier preferred Criminal Misc. Application No. 22005 of 2023 which was allowed to be withdrawn by this Court vide order dated 12.12.2023 and while allowing the said Application, liberty was granted to the Applicant to file Application afresh after a period of eight months if the trial did not progress satisfactorily.
5.1
It has been brought to the notice of this Court that the trial is in progress and inasmuch as seventy percent of the trial is already over.
In view of the same, this Court is not inclined to entertain the present Application being a Successive Bail Aplication.
6. So far as the argument made by learned Advocate for the Aplicant to the effect that the case of the proseciton is concocted, it cannot be accepted at this stage.
The age of the prosecutrix was 14 Years and 10 Months at the relevant time.
She has consistently given the same version as regards the incident at various places.
There is no reason for this Court to disbelieve her version at NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/24129/2024 ORDER DATED: 06/02/2025 undefined this stage.

Having Surajsinh Vajubha Rathod vs State Of Gujarat on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24819231/
2 regard to the same, no case is made out.

entities.text: Surajsinh Vajubha Rathod vs State Of Gujarat on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Aplication is dismissed.
(M. R. MENGDEY,J) J.N.W / 71
